## Sequencing and reviewability

M1 is a contained, unconnected installation safety responsibility with explicit unchanged-public-behavior limits, tests for selected-root/state transaction and intervening-write recovery, and independent milestone review. M2 connects the authoring inventory, all named consumers, resource projections, public installer guards/replacement, candidate metadata and selected authority navigation in one complete acceptance boundary. This dependency avoids prematurely rejecting the currently released inventory or leaving competing public authoring contracts. M2 has a large file count, but the exact source/consumer disposition table, logical review facets, complete-milestone judgment and coherent rollback requirement make the boundary assessable. If that responsibility cannot remain reviewable, the plan requires replanning rather than treating partial public cutovers as completion.

Rollback preserves user files, historical records/ADRs, unrelated state and previously independent writes. The helper-only M1 result is explicitly insufficient for public installation. Required governance/source edits remain under their owners and separate review; an implementation discovery requiring a changed behavior or milestone boundary returns upstream. Later consolidation families are explicit and cannot absorb unfinished present consumer reconciliation.

## Traceability and verification adequacy

DES-SR-01–20, SYS-SR-01–09, affected Workflow coordination, TNI-DES-01–06 and retained hash/state invariants map into named M1/M2 work and TG-01–07. All eight source-qualified installer boundaries and INT-001–03 have local/public integrated allocation; the plan consumes their exact IDs without recreating their normative scope. The adopted model profile allocates proof in this primary plan rather than restoring a standalone test-spec stage or ledger.

TG-FINAL-01 tests assembled authoring, affected-model and legacy subject handoff, installed conditional guidance and migrated ownership; MW-01/02 require independent semantic assessment because parsing, resource presence and identifier counts cannot establish those claims. TG-FINAL-02 and MW-03 require the real CLI and exact candidate for successful managed upgrade, original-hash rejection contrast, modified/unsafe roots, OpenCode multi-root aliases, unrelated state preservation, process interruption, caught/state-write/rollback failures, competing writes and coherent backup recovery. Helper-only, mock-only and dry-run-only proof are expressly excluded for these composed claims. Distinct contract-derived bytes and fixture bases prevent circular oracles.

The plan retains meaningful negative/regression protection and requires group-level maintenance rationale before replacement/removal. TG-05 expressly retains the pairwise example ownership check that the existing overlap validator cannot establish. Source, archive, installed-resource and public-command checks cover different boundaries; the manual procedures have responsible assessors, durable evidence and freshness conditions. All required integrated proof and follow-up dispositions precede fresh independent final whole-change Code Review, followed by distinct final Verify. Milestone reviews cannot replace that checkpoint.

## Source and execution feasibility

Inspected source confirms current adapter inventories and skill-validation consumer sets still contain the two retiring authors; M2 allocates their owning modules and corresponding test suites. The final author allocation also names the retained boundary-first-proof-model mapping consumer and current prose author-role validator, while distinguishing historical artifact/protocol/measurement IDs from live inventory assumptions. These bounded dependencies preserve the approved responsibility and proof boundary. The boundary-resource manifest identifies compact/feature projections for the retiring spec consumer; both source/projection owners are allocated. The existing adapter builder and local candidate metadata helper provide measured archives and metadata without inventing release provenance. The package is 0.5.1 with local-release-candidate metadata, so V5/V8 candidate verification is appropriately mandatory while V9 publication gates depend on separately owned release authority and required artifacts. No existing unsupported release command is represented as a passing current requirement.

Concrete V1–V8 commands and changed-path selector union cover the owned Node, source/projection, structural/selector, adapter, packaging and record surfaces. New helper tests are planned at a named discovery path; affected shared installer extraction triggers the full existing public suite. Actual generation and controlled installation must occur during implementation, not be replaced by this feasibility assessment. Source paths discovered as directly required callers must be explicitly reconciled or returned upstream; unallocated unrelated behavior is excluded.

## Evidence and limits

The complete primary plan was read. Current CLI context confirmed its registered identity, all four approved model subjects and independent-review activity; Design r5 applicability remains current and f1–f5 remain resolved with preserved origins. Author evidence reports plan prose/readability, link/allocation checks and their limits; these support inspectability and are not approval or executed implementation proof. The 13 original Target-native init prose errors remain failed/current evidence. The plan requires exact baseline comparison, blocks new errors and leaves final applicability to the responsible assessor rather than silently waiving full-file failures.

No implementation tests, generated archives, installation, fault injection or final verification were run during this Delivery review. Source inspection and the plan's explicit commands/procedures establish a credible proof allocation only. After save, run `node scripts/validate-record-store.mjs docs/changes/2026-09-08-unified-design-authoring-and-bounded-model-consolidation/change.json` and `git diff --check`. Recording and those checks establish neither implementation nor workflow readiness by themselves. Direct-source inspection replaces reliance on the known-stale project map for this bounded assessment.

## Independence provenance

Independent Delivery assessment by concrete task /root/independent_design_review. Primary-agent/plan authored the exact primary plan; reviewer authored none of it. Prior service as the independent Design reviewer is source familiarity, not plan authorship or a substitute for this fresh Delivery judgment. Reviewer read the complete plan and relevant current source contracts, has not edited governed content or implementation, and treats author self-checks as evidence only.
